body: Claude: **must-fix**: Re-anchoring on the remaining cached window fixes the never-requeried cases, but it puts no floor on the resulting spacing, so a short window compresses all five maintenance points into it. `TEST(mdns_service_update_short_window)` demonstrates it: with 5 s left until `until`, `lifetime` is 5 s and the points land at 9.00/9.25/9.50/9.75/10.00 s, i.e. four multicast maintenance queries for one record inside 750 ms, and the 2% jitter (100 ms) cannot spread them. With 1 s left they are 50 ms apart with 20 ms of jitter. Each dispatch runs the full `mdns_maintenance_query()` body: a `dns_query_go()` query on the mDNS scope plus, on completion, `mdns_browser_revisit_cache()`, which re-looks-up the cache, diffs the whole `sb->dns_services` list and emits a varlink notification. None of those queries can plausibly be answered and re-cached before `until` passes. This is new relative to the base revision, where a short window made every point come out in the past and the schedule fell through to the query-less 100% state, so nothing was sent; and it is reached routinely, since `dns_add_new_service()` computes `lifetime` from `until - now()` for a subscription that may start anywhere in a record's cached lifetime. RFC 6762 section 5.2 intends the points to be spread over 20% of a real TTL, which is also what makes the 2% variation meaningful for de-synchronising hosts on the link. Please bound the compressed case, e.g. require a minimum absolute gap between consecutive points, or fall through to the 100% cache revisit when `lifetime` is below a small threshold, so it degrades to one refresh rather than four.
